issues.description: Switch from req.stream.read() to req.bounded_stream.read() changes semantics; falcon already enforces Content-Length on stream, and bounded_stream will block waiting for the missing byte
issues.detail: The PR replaces `body = req.stream.read()` with `body = req.bounded_stream.read()` in examples/things_advanced.py to make the 'Content-Length: 1 with empty body' case return 400. However, `bounded_stream` will read exactly `content_length` bytes; with WSGI test infrastructure that returns an empty body it may return b'' (so the test passes), but on a real WSGI server `bounded_stream.read()` can block waiting for the missing byte from the client. The original `req.stream` already wraps the WSGI input with the same bounded reader for non-chunked requests, so the change either does nothing useful or introduces a hang risk in production. The 400 behavior the test asserts is being produced by the test harness, not by anything the real example reliably does.

issues.description: FAQ example contains an incorrect StorageError.handle signature change in README, breaking the documented error handler contract
issues.detail: In README.rst the `StorageError.handle` signature is changed from `(ex, req, resp, params)` to `(req, resp, ex, params)`. Falcon's `add_error_handler` historically expected `(ex, req, resp, params)` for the legacy signature and `(req, resp, ex, params)` is the newer one — but this change is bundled into a documentation-only PR with no discussion and no corresponding code/test backing it. If the surrounding README/code is meant to mirror the existing example, this reordering should not be silently included in a 'tests for POST' PR. It also makes the README diverge from any reader's working copy of the same example.

issues.description: FAQ code sample has style/syntax issues: stray trailing comma in headers list, `assert(...)` parenthesized as call, and PostTest reads stream incorrectly
issues.detail: In docs/user/faq.rst, `headers = [('Content-Length', '1'),]` has an unnecessary trailing comma inside square brackets that reads oddly in published docs. `assert(result.status == falcon.HTTP_400)` is the well-known anti-pattern that turns assert into a function call (works, but lints/flake8 flag it as E275/redundant parens). Also, `req.stream.read(req.content_length or 0)` is awkward since the outer `if req.content_length in (None, 0)` branch already returns 200 — meaning the `or 0` is dead code. Tighten this snippet before it becomes copy-pasted by users.

issues.description: New POST test does not exercise the case the PR claims to add (the 400 path is driven by transport behavior, not example logic)
issues.detail: resp4 sends `Content-Length: 1` with `body=''`. The example code path in things_advanced.py only raises HTTPBadRequest('Empty request body') when `body` from the stream read is falsy. With `bounded_stream.read()` and an empty WSGI body, what is actually returned depends on the simulate_post implementation — the test passes because of testing harness behavior, not because the example correctly handles a mismatched Content-Length in production. The test therefore documents a behavior the example does not actually guarantee. Either change the example to validate `req.content_length` explicitly, or assert on a realistic scenario (e.g., POST with truly empty body and no Content-Length).

issues.description: README diff bundles unrelated cosmetic refactors with the test PR
issues.detail: The README.rst changes include extensive reformatting unrelated to the stated goal: import reordering, removal of blank lines after class declarations, switching `str(result.status_code) + ' ' + result.reason` to `falcon.code_to_http_status(...)`, `%`-formatting to `.format()`, and rewrapped multi-line string literals. None of these belong in a PR titled 'add POST request tests for the things_advanced example'. They make the diff hard to review, hide the actual behavioral change (stream -> bounded_stream), and increase merge-conflict risk. Split these into a separate cleanup PR.

issues.description: No ASGI coverage added despite the checklist claiming WSGI+ASGI parity
issues.detail: test_things_advanced takes an `asgi` parameter but the new resp3/resp4 calls always use `testing.simulate_post(advanced.app, ...)` — the same WSGI app — without parameterizing on the ASGI variant the rest of the test presumably uses. If `advanced.app` is conditionally WSGI/ASGI via the fixture, that's fine, but it should be explicit. Additionally, `bounded_stream` semantics differ between WSGI and ASGI (the ASGI version is a coroutine-style reader); the change in things_advanced.py was not validated on the ASGI path.

issues.description: Missing towncrier news fragment despite checklist tick
issues.detail: The PR checklist claims `docs/_newsfragments/` was updated, but no such file appears in the diff. For a docs/test change this may be acceptable, but the project requires it per CONTRIBUTING. Either add `678.misc.rst` (or appropriate type) or remove the unsupported checklist claim.

issues.description: FAQ heading and section placement: new Q&A is inserted mid-file without cross-reference from the testing docs
issues.detail: The new FAQ entry 'How can I set header fields when simulating requests?' is a useful addition but is not cross-referenced from the testing module's Sphinx docs. Users searching for `simulate_post` headers won't find it. Add a `.. seealso::` link from the testing reference page, or move the example into the `falcon.testing` docstring where it belongs.

issues.description: Magic token 'custom-token' and path '/1337/things' are unexplained
issues.detail: The new test uses `Authorization: custom-token` and path `/1337/things` without a comment explaining why these values pass AuthMiddleware (the example's `_token_is_valid` returns True unconditionally) or what `1337` represents. A one-line comment would prevent confusion when this test breaks during future middleware changes.

dissents.topic: Is the stream -> bounded_stream change a bug fix or a regression?

positions.position: It's a latent regression: bounded_stream can block on real WSGI servers waiting for missing bytes when Content-Length exceeds actual body. The example used to handle empty bodies via the `if not body:` check; now it relies on the bounded reader returning empty, which is harness-specific.

It's an improvement: bounded_stream is the documented best practice in falcon for limiting reads to declared Content-Length, preventing slowloris-style reads. The 'block on missing bytes' concern is the server's job to time out, not the framework's.

dissents.topic: Should the README cosmetic changes be split out?

positions.position: Yes — bundling unrelated reformat with behavioral changes violates 'one PR, one purpose' and makes future bisects harder.
No — the README and example were already inconsistent; fixing both in one go reduces churn and the reformatting is auto-generated by ruff/black so it's noise-equivalent.

dissents.topic: Does the new test actually test the example's logic?

positions.position: No — the 400 response is produced by harness/stream behavior, not by a Content-Length validation branch in the example. The test would pass even if the example were silently broken on real servers.
Yes enough — end-to-end status code is what users care about; the test pins observed behavior and will catch regressions in either layer.

review.summary: The PR has a clear surface goal (add POST tests) but bundles three loosely-related changes: a behavioral switch from `req.stream.read()` to `req.bounded_stream.read()` in the example, extensive cosmetic reformatting of README.rst, and a new FAQ entry. The headline concern is that the new 400-on-empty-body test passes because of harness behavior around bounded_stream rather than any explicit Content-Length validation in the example — meaning the test documents a behavior the example does not robustly guarantee on real WSGI servers. Secondary issues: the README diff contains an unrelated error-handler signature change that shouldn't ride along, the FAQ snippet has lint-level issues (`assert(...)`, dead `or 0`, stray trailing comma), and ASGI parity for the bounded_stream change is unverified. Recommendation: split the README cleanup into its own PR, either make the example validate Content-Length explicitly or change the test to a scenario the example actually handles, and tighten the FAQ snippet before merge.
